notes: kb/Work PB5070 owns the fix (labelRecordsClause and valueOfClause are word lists no binder reads); it lists 1985-FMT-VII.3.9.2 and 1985-FMT-XIII.3.2.2, not this row. §1985:VII.3.2.2 prints FD file-name-1 with the optional clauses BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD (three forms), LABEL { RECORD IS | RECORDS ARE } { STANDARD | OMITTED }, VALUE OF { implementor-name-1 IS { data-name-2 | literal-1 } } ..., DATA { RECORD IS | RECORDS ARE } { data-name-3 } ..., LINAGE and CODE-SET, closed by a period; §1985:VII.3.2.3 SR2 lets the clauses come in any order. Implemented at 85: fileDescriptionEntry takes any number of fileDescriptionClause alternatives in any order and requires the period; BindFileSection binds each clause through FileDescriptionClauseAdmitted (the Rows table: LINAGE and CODE-SET on a sequential file only, a file control clause in the FD is COBOL2604), BindBlockContainsClause, BindRecordClause, BindLinageClause (FOOTING, TOP, BOTTOM only in the printed sequence) and BindCodeSetClause; ScreenClauseRepetition refuses any clause written twice (COBOL2423) and VisitUnrecognizedDataClause any other word (COBOL1970, RECORDING MODE probed); the later editions' additions are refused at 85 (BYTES and a second CODE-SET alphabet or FOR phrase by VisitRecordClause and VisitCodeSetClause, COBOL0900; EXTERNAL AS literal COBOL0900; FORMAT COBOL1705). Probed at 85: an FD with all seven clauses, the same clauses in reverse order with every optional word dropped, and an FD with no clause compile and run. Not implemented: the operands of two clauses. labelRecordsClause ends in (STANDARD | OMITTED | cobolWord+) and valueOfClause is VALUE OF (cobolWord | literal | IS)+, and BindFileSection has no arm for either, so LABEL RECORDS ARE IGNORED, LABEL RECORD IS LBL1 LBL2, VALUE OF "X" (no implementor-name-1) and VALUE OF IS IS IS compile clean at 85. Two neighbours owned elsewhere: BLOCK CONTAINS 2 TO 2 RECORDS is refused at 85 by the 2023 ordered-pair rule (PB5115, row 1985-FMT-VII.3.3.2), and RECORD CONTAINS 5 TO 5 CHARACTERS the same way (this pass's record on 1985-FMT-VII.3.8.2). Transcription: specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md underlines CHARACTERS in this format's BLOCK CONTAINS clause; the printed page (PDF page 396, folio VII-22, rendered) and §1985:VII.3.3.2 do not, so CHARACTERS is the default option of the braces (§1985:IV.2.1.4) and BLOCK CONTAINS 10 with neither word, which the compiler accepts, conforms. The witness writes BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD CONTAINS, LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD and DATA RECORD IS on one FD and reads two records back.

next.reason: §1985:VII.3.2.2, the sequential file description entry, writes out BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD, LABEL RECORDS, VALUE OF, DATA RECORDS, LINAGE and CODE-SET. Its 2023 counterpart is §2023:13.4.5.2 'Format 1 (sequential)', which §2023:13.4.5.3 SR5 names ('Format 1 is the file description entry for a sequential file'); it writes BLOCK CONTAINS and CODE-SET in line and takes the RECORD and LINAGE clauses by reference to §2023:13.18.43.2 and §2023:13.18.34.2. It has no LABEL RECORDS, VALUE OF or DATA RECORDS clause (in 1985 the subjects of §1985:VII.3.2.4 GR2, 'the DATA RECORDS clause, the LABEL RECORDS clause'), so a 1985 FD using them is refused; it also adds FORMAT and a wider CODE-SET. A compile-time difference, no exception condition: CHANGED. The clause-order rule carries its own record (1985 SR2). The BLOCK CONTAINS and CODE-SET clauses Format 1 writes in line are restated by their own clause formats, §2023:13.18.10.2 and §2023:13.18.13.2, which therefore state part of the entry's syntax too.
